documents.title: TypeSpec pagination
documents.guidanceExcerpt: To enable pagination for an operation the first step is to decorate it with the `@list` decorator and have the return type contain a property decorated with `@pageItems`.
documents.applicableGuidance: Paged operations use @list, identify page items, and identify the server-provided next link.
documents.evidence: The changed operation has @list, while OutboundRuleListResult identifies value with @pageItems and nextLink with @nextLink.

documents.title: ARM long-running operations
documents.guidanceExcerpt: The `ArmResourceActionAsync` template uses `ArmLroLocationHeader` by default. The `FinalResult` should match the response type of the action.
documents.applicableGuidance: An ARM async action's logical final result matches its response type.
documents.evidence: The action retains Response = OutboundRuleListResult while adding paging metadata.

documents.title: Adding a Stable Version when the Last Version was Preview
documents.section: Making changes to your TypeSpec spec
documents.guidanceExcerpt: For any type with an `@added(p)` decorator, delete the type. Remove the replaced preview version from the version enum.
documents.applicableGuidance: A stable version replacing a preview removes the preview member and reverses preview-only additions.
documents.evidence: RecoveryServicesBackup retains v2026_01_31_preview beside v2026_02_01 and retains preview-only declarations with @removed(v2026_02_01).

documents.title: Clients
documents.guidanceExcerpt: Customizations SHOULD always be made in a file named `client.tsp` alongside `main.tsp`.
documents.applicableGuidance: Client hierarchy customizations belong in client.tsp.
documents.evidence: The edited @@clientLocation declarations remain in back-compatible.tsp.

findings.title: The replaced preview version remains in the stable-version history
findings.summary: RecoveryServicesBackup keeps v2026_01_31_preview and its preview-only declarations while appending v2026_02_01, contrary to the documented stable-after-preview workflow.
evidence: The guide says to remove the replaced preview member and delete preview-only additions.
The PR instead retains the preview member and scopes preview-only declarations out with @removed(v2026_02_01).

findings.title: Edited client customizations remain outside client.tsp
findings.summary: The client guide says customizations should always be authored in client.tsp, but the edited @@clientLocation declarations are in back-compatible.tsp.
evidence: The decorators correctly customize client hierarchy and language scope.
Their placement does not follow the documented client.tsp convention.

documents.title: Azure.Core decorators
documents.guidanceExcerpt: Overrides the final state value for an operation. The supported values include `location`.
documents.applicableGuidance: Use @useFinalStateVia("location") to select the Location-based LRO final-state strategy.
documents.evidence: The changed LRO helpers apply @Azure.Core.useFinalStateVia("location").

documents.title: ARM long-running operations
documents.guidanceExcerpt: The `ArmResourceActionAsync` template uses `ArmLroLocationHeader` by default. The `FinalResult` should match the response type of the action.
documents.applicableGuidance: Location-polled ARM actions use matching Location headers, Retry-After, and logical final-result types.
documents.evidence: The helpers use ArmLroLocationHeader<FinalResult = ...>, RetryAfterHeader, and concrete action result types.

documents.title: Azure Core no-openapi rule
documents.guidanceExcerpt: Azure specs should not be using decorators from @typespec/openapi or @azure-tools/typespec-autorest because other emitters will not be able to understand them.
documents.applicableGuidance: Represent behavior with emitter-independent TypeSpec and Azure constructs instead of raw OpenAPI extensions.
documents.evidence: The PR removes raw x-ms-long-running-operation extensions and replaces them with Azure.Core LRO metadata.

documents.title: Azure Core no-enum rule
documents.guidanceExcerpt: Using a union with the base scalar (`string`, `int32`, `int64`, etc.) as a variant instead of an enum makes it extensible.
documents.applicableGuidance: Use an open union containing the base scalar and named known values for an extensible service value.
documents.evidence: CloudHsmClusterSkuName changes from a suppressed enum to a union containing string and two named variants with unchanged wire values.

documents.title: Adding a Stable Version when the Last Version was Preview

documents.applicableGuidance: A stable release replacing a preview removes the preview member and retargets promoted changes.

documents.title: Private Endpoints
documents.section: Defining a Private Endpoint Connection Resource
documents.guidanceExcerpt: Resource providers that support private endpoint connections must declare a private endpoint connection resource type and use the standard `PrivateEndpoints` interface to expose operations.
documents.applicableGuidance: Private endpoint connections extend PrivateEndpointConnectionResource and use PrivateEndpoints operations.
documents.evidence: The PR manually models PrivateEndpointConnection as ProxyResource and uses generic ArmResource operations.

documents.title: Private Links
documents.guidanceExcerpt: Resource providers that support private link resources must declare a private link resource type and use the standard `PrivateLinks` interface to expose operations.
documents.applicableGuidance: Private-link discovery uses the standard PrivateLink model and PrivateLinks operation interface.
documents.evidence: The PR manually models PrivateLinkResource as ProxyResource and uses generic read/list templates.

documents.title: TypeSpec Client Generator Core decorators
documents.guidanceExcerpt: Set whether a model property should be flattened or not. This decorator is not recommended to use for green field services.
documents.applicableGuidance: Do not add legacy flattening to newly introduced API models without an existing compatibility requirement.
documents.evidence: The new private endpoint and private link resource properties are flattened for AutoRest and C#.

findings.title: The stable version retains the replaced preview version
findings.summary: The enum keeps v2025_10_01_preview while appending v2026_03_01, contrary to the stable-after-preview procedure.
evidence: The documented workflow removes the replaced preview member and retargets promoted changes to stable.

findings.title: Private endpoint connections bypass the standard templates
findings.summary: PrivateEndpointConnection is manually modeled and uses generic operations instead of PrivateEndpointConnectionResource and PrivateEndpoints.
evidence: The official private-endpoint guide requires the standard resource base and PrivateEndpoints interface.

findings.title: Private-link discovery bypasses the standard templates
findings.summary: PrivateLinkResource is manually modeled and uses generic operations instead of PrivateLink and PrivateLinks.
evidence: The official private-link guide requires the standard model and PrivateLinks interface.

findings.title: Legacy flattening is applied to newly introduced models
findings.summary: New private endpoint and private link resource properties use a legacy decorator that the reference does not recommend for greenfield types.
evidence: The changed types are newly introduced, so they have no prior flattened SDK contract to preserve.

documents.title: TypeSpec Client Generator Core decorators
documents.guidanceExcerpt: Change the operation location in the client. If the target client is not defined, use `string` to indicate a new client name.
documents.applicableGuidance: A string target and a supported language scope are valid clientLocation arguments.
documents.evidence: The Python-specific @@clientLocation calls use documented string targets and scopes.

documents.guidanceExcerpt: The TypeSpec should represent the current state of the API.
documents.applicableGuidance: Delete declarations that should exist in no API version; use @removed only when retaining them for earlier versions.
documents.evidence: The removed NFSv2 declarations existed only in the latest unreleased version and should no longer exist in any version.

documents.title: TypeSpec Client Generator Core decorators
documents.guidanceExcerpt: Customize a method's signature in the generated client SDK. Currently, only parameter signature customization is supported.
documents.applicableGuidance: Use a language-scoped override operation to customize parameter order.
documents.evidence: The Go-only @@override is in client.tsp and reorders the delete operation parameters.

documents.title: ARM resource types and modeling
documents.guidanceExcerpt: Resources are modeled in TypeSpec by choosing a base resource type, defining rp-specific properties, and optionally mixing in standard envelope properties. Child resources usually use the `ProxyResource<TProperties>` as their base resource type.
documents.applicableGuidance: A resource-shaped child chooses a documented ARM base and declares its parent instead of reconstructing the envelope in a legacy plain model.
documents.evidence: ConnectionAnalyzer is a plain model with Legacy.customAzureResource and manually repeated ARM envelope fields.

documents.title: ARM resource operations
documents.guidanceExcerpt: Custom actions define any operations over resources outside the simple CRUDL (Create, Read, Update, Delete, List) or lifecycle operations described above.
documents.applicableGuidance: CRUDL uses ArmResourceRead, ArmResourceCreateOrReplace, ArmTagsPatch or ArmCustomPatch, ArmResourceDelete, and ArmResourceListByParent; actions are reserved for behavior outside CRUDL.
documents.evidence: ConnectionAnalyzer PUT, GET, PATCH, and DELETE use Legacy.RoutedOperations action helpers, while list is manually routed.

findings.title: Connection Analyzer does not use a documented ARM base resource type
findings.summary: The resource-type guidance says an ARM resource is modeled by choosing a base type, but ConnectionAnalyzer is a plain model marked with Legacy.customAzureResource.
evidence: The documented child pattern uses @parentResource and ProxyResource<TProperties> with ResourceNameParameter.
ConnectionAnalyzer manually repeats id, name, type, location, tags, systemData, and properties.

findings.title: Connection Analyzer does not use the documented ARM resource operation templates
findings.summary: The new resource-style CRUD and list operations use legacy action helpers and manual routes instead of standard ARM resource-operation templates.
evidence: Official guidance reserves actions for behavior outside CRUDL.
Exact modern templates exist for all five ConnectionAnalyzer lifecycle operations; only /query is a genuine custom action.

documents.title: Azure.ResourceManager decorators
documents.guidanceExcerpt: This decorator is used either on a namespace or a version enum value to indicate the version of the Azure Resource Manager common-types to use for refs in emitted Swagger files.
documents.applicableGuidance: A version enum member may select the ARM common-types version it emits.
documents.evidence: Both changed preview members select Azure.ResourceManager.CommonTypes.Versions.v5.

documents.title: arm-common-types-version rule
documents.guidanceExcerpt: If the common types version is updated in later versions, the decorator should appear on each version enum member.
documents.applicableGuidance: Services with varying historical common-types versions use per-version decorators.
documents.evidence: The project already uses per-version declarations and the PR preserves that pattern.

documents.title: TypeSpec Client Generator Core decorators
documents.guidanceExcerpt: Overrides the generated name for client SDK elements including clients, methods, parameters, unions, models, enums, and model properties.
documents.applicableGuidance: Use a language-scoped @clientName to preserve SDK identifiers without changing service-facing values.
documents.evidence: Six augment decorators target union members, provide released Java identifiers, and use the supported java scope.

documents.title: Clients
documents.section: Customizations and Renaming the Client Name
documents.guidanceExcerpt: Customizations SHOULD always be made in a file named `client.tsp` alongside `main.tsp`. This can be achieved with the augment decorator: `@clientName`.
documents.applicableGuidance: Client-name compatibility customizations use augment decorators in client.tsp.
documents.evidence: The changed @@clientName declarations are in client.tsp and leave serialized union values unchanged.
